label: Delimiter boundary (last original token, <DEL>, first copy step) in long sequences, absolute step 8-10
explanation: Fires in a narrow window around the delimiter: the last original token (t=L-1), the <DEL> step (53% of mass, 30% fire rate), and the first copy output step (recall_idx 0/1). It depends on absolute position too, so it is almost confined to long sequences (L=8,9 carry 90% of mass; L<=5 essentially never) and absolute steps t=7-10. Strongest activations sit on <DEL> and the step just after it in L=7-9 sequences. It does not fire during the early original phase (t<=5), in later copy steps (recall_idx>=3), or in short sequences. Within the window only about half of steps fire. Which ones fire depends on token content in a way no single token variable captures (first_tok a and digit count give only mild lift), so precision tops out around 0.53. Dev: P 0.53, R 0.81, F1 0.64, mass recall 0.89.
